text: Fort Oglethorpe is a city primarily located in Catoosa County with some areas extending into Walker County in the U.S. state of Georgia. As of the 2020 census, the city had a population of 10,423, with 3,994 households and 2,240 families. The city covers a total area of 13.9 square miles (36.0 km²), all of which is land, and is situated at 34°56′44″N 85°14′44″W (34.94556°N 85.24556°W). It lies 9 miles (14 km) south of Chattanooga, Tennessee, via U.S. Route 27, which continues 18 miles (29 km) south to LaFayette, Georgia. The Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park occupies the southern two-thirds of the city. The city is part of the Chattanooga, Tennessee–Georgia Metropolitan Statistical Area. Fort Oglethorpe was established on land originally owned by William Hamilton Hargrave and his wife Amelia Cecilia Strange-Hargrave, a Confederate soldier and landowner, near the Chickamauga National Battlefield. The U.S. Army established a cavalry post at the site in 1902, later naming it Fort Oglethorpe after James Oglethorpe, founder of the Colony of Georgia. During and after World War I (1917–1920), the fort served as a detention camp for civilian internees and prisoners of war. During World War II, it functioned as a war-time induction and processing center and again housed prisoners of war, and also served as a major training center for the Women's Army Corps. The post land was declared surplus in 1947 and returned to civilian use, leading to the incorporation of the town in 1949. As of the 2000 U.S. census, the population was 6,940, with 2,873 households and 1,881 families, and a population density of 532.6 inhabitants per square mile (205.6/km²). The racial makeup was 93.14% White, 2.38% African American, 0.19% Native American, 2.07% Asian, 0.03% Pacific Islander, 0.56% from other races, and 1.63% from two or more races, with 1.41% identifying as Hispanic or Latino. Household data showed 29.3% had children under 18, 47.0% were married couples, 15.0% had a female householder with no husband, and 34.5% were non-families; 30.6% were made up of individuals, and 13.3% had someone 65 or older living alone. The average household size was 2.29, and average family size was 2.86. The age distribution included 22.8% under 18, 9.5% aged 18–24, 26.3% aged 25–44, 21.8% aged 45–64, and 19.6% aged 65 or older, with a median age of 38. For every 100 females, there were 82.2 males, and for every 100 females aged 18 and over, there were 76.9 males. The median household income was $32,095, median family income was $40,643, male median income was $28,160, and female median income was $21,141. The per capita income was $16,288, with 11.5% of families and 17.4% of the population below the poverty line, including 30.8% of those under 18 and 11.3% of those 65 or older. As of circa 2024, 9,013 residents lived in Catoosa County and 250 lived in Walker County. The portion in Catoosa County is within the Catoosa County School District, which includes Lakeview–Fort Oglethorpe High School, while the Walker County portion is within the Walker County School District.
